summary: Host only: nothing was built for, flashed to, run on or read from the phone, and no decision was requested. From the real payload bytes (capstone) and the NAT-030 instruction-level model, the code the kernel runs after assembly checkpoint 5 up to the first safe C checkpoint (11) was listed, and a resume at checkpoint 5 was designed and checked in the model: the stub branches MMU-off to the kernel's own MMU-enable block 28 bytes before the checkpoint-5 macro (0xfffffff00743e454) with slot[2] set to 11 under a civac/dsb/str/dsb/civac/dsb sequence and every live register and SP restored, which makes the trampoline ideas (NAT-029 'restore M in the stub', the 725-NOP sled) unnecessary because the loader image (about 0x801a0000) is outside the kernel's TTBR0 identity range 0x9e1400000..0x9fe200000. The resumed run equals the uninterrupted run in registers, system registers and RAM for two junk values with no taint violation; the obvious resume at site+60 with the MMU off fails; an unchanged slot stops again; a wrong x21 diverges. The model reaches the call of loader_checkpoint(10) in 275 steps after the resume (arm_set_kernel_tbi, memmove, loader_checkpoint) and stops at the first SIMD instruction in cpu_data_init+0x10. Statically the first PE_init_platform(0, args) call path (46 functions without the panic and vm_initialized edges) has no system-register access, no svc/hvc/smc, no tlbi/dc/ic and two jump-table indirect branches; gic_v3_irq_quiesce is a no-op because gicd_base is 0 and its only direct writer is outside the path. The C path arrives MMU-on in a private 2 MiB Normal-WB block (MAIR byte 0 = 0xff) and needs a stub prologue that clears SCTLR_EL1.M; it is not resumable. Not established: any behaviour of the S24 past checkpoint 5.
